newsitem.title: ECUADOR: Ecuador hikes liquor, tobacco tax to fight vice.
newsitem.headline: Ecuador hikes liquor, tobacco tax to fight vice.

text.p: Ecuadorans who pay $295 for a bottle of imported liquor can thank their president for helping save them from destruction at their own hands, according to President Abdala Bucaram.

The president said he decided to defend his citizens from vice by slapping a 1,000 percent tax on imported liquor and cigarettes. "Ecuadorans have to know that drinking and smoking lead to nothing but destruction," he said late on Thursday.

With the import tariff, a bottle of whiskey will cost $295 compared with some $15 under the old "libertine" system, Bucaram told reporters. He said he felt he had a duty to prevent Ecuadorans from falling prey to drink and cigarettes.

"One cannot say it is a right because if I see a citizen -- and I am the president of the republic -- pointing a gun to his head and (who) wants to commit suicide, my obligation is to say 'don't do it' and fight to prevent it," he said.

The populist leader has dabbled in upholding Ecuador's moral standards before. Early in his political career he zipped around Guayaquil on a motorcycle stopping young women and unstitching their miniskirts' hems to make the skirts longer.

Bucaram, who boasted during his successful presidential race that "I do whatever the hell I like," campaigned by jumping from a helicopter in a Batman outfit. Since taking office he has recorded and performed his rock album "A Madman in Love" accompanied by sleek young female singers.
He also had lunch at the presidential palace with Lorena Bobbitt, who became notorious in the United States for cutting off her then-husband's penis during a domestic quarrel.
